clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: T-tests were used to examine whether PD deviation scores were significantly different from a null distribution. Pearson correlations (with FDR correction) tested associations between deviation scores and disease duration, as well as cognitive scores. Regional contribution to deviations was assessed using leave-one-region-out analysis (Δr²). Regional functional differences between PD and age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n=17,400) were quantified using Cohen's d effect sizes. Multiple comparison corrections were applied using either Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) or Bonferroni-Holm procedures.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Age-related changes in resting-state functional measures colocalized with multiple neurotransmitter systems; PD patients showed significant deviations from normative colocalization patterns across serotonergic, dopaminergic, GABAergic, cholinergic, and glutamatergic systems; deviation in LCOR-GABAA colocalization correlated with disease duration.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Age-related decreases in fALFF, LCOR, and GCOR were widespread across cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions. Group-level aging effects colocalized significantly (pFDR < .05) with serotonergic, dopaminergic, noradrenergic, and glutamatergic neurotransmission for fALFF and LCOR, and with noradrenergic transmission for GCOR. Individual-level colocalization strengths showed significant age-related changes (pBonferroni-Holm < .05) for most neurotransmitter systems, with age explaining up to 3%, 4%, and 1% of colocalization variance for fALFF (with NMDA and SERT), LCOR (with SERT), and GCOR (with VAChT), respectively. Variance in colocalization increased with age for multiple neurotransmitter systems (11/14 for fALFF, 14/15 for LCOR, 7/11 for GCOR showed higher variance in older vs younger subpopulations). PD patients showed significant deviations from normative models: for fALFF, lower colocalization with serotonergic, GABAergic, muscarinic, and glutamatergic systems; for LCOR and GCOR, lower colocalization with serotonergic, dopaminergic, GABAergic, histaminergic, noradrenergic, glutamatergic, and cholinergic systems. Deviation in LCOR-GABAA colocalization was negatively correlated with disease duration (Pearson's r = -0.38, pFDR = .027). Regional contributions to PD deviations were primarily in basal ganglia, insula, occipital regions, subcallosal areas, thalamus, and basal forebrain. Regional contributions for glutamatergic deviations significantly correlated with regional alterations in PD (pFDR < .05).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: UK Biobank biases include high average socioeconomic status and low alcohol/tobacco consumption; PD severity measures (UPDRS, Hoehn & Yahr stages) were not available, only disease duration and limited cognitive scores; PD medication effects may have contributed to observed patterns but previous work suggests these effects are small compared to PD itself; PET maps from differently aged healthy populations may introduce bias as receptor/transporter distributions may change with aging; participants with mild depression (F32) were included to avoid bias (12.32% of cohort had ICD-10: F32 reference)
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: The studied cohort was recruited as a representative sample of healthy UK residents... Given the prevalence of mild depressive symptoms in the UK population of 11% and the fact that 12.32% of our analyzed participants from the UK Biobank have a reference to ICD-10: F32, their exclusion would have biased the cohort. PD appearance and progression is highly heterogeneous. Because no scores for PD severity [i.e., Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale or Hoehn & Yahr stages] and only a limited number of cognitive scores were available, we could only roughly approximate PD severity based on disease duration. Because PD medication is known to affect measures of brain function, it might have contributed to some of the effects observed in the PD cohort... Additional healthy control biases in the UK Biobank include a high average socioeconomic status and low alcohol and tobacco consumption... Using PET maps from differently aged healthy populations might have introduced a further bias into our findings because proteomics such as receptor and transporter distributions may change during aging.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study used a novel approach combining normative modeling with spatial colocalization analysis between functional MRI measures and neurotransmitter maps from the JuSpace toolbox (19 distinct neurotransmitter maps from independent PET/SPECT studies). The neuromorphometrics atlas (119 regions) was used for parcellation. Leave-one-region-out analysis was employed to identify regional contributions (Δr²) to deviation patterns. The study included sensitivity analyses controlling for age-related atrophy by regressing out individual voxelwise gray matter volumes and repeating all analyses.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study represents a methodological innovation by combining normative modeling with spatial colocalization analysis of functional MRI and neurotransmitter maps. The UK Biobank dataset provided a large normative sample (n=25,917) spanning ages approximately 44-82 years (based on subgroup ranges mentioned for variance analysis). The study included 19 neurotransmitter maps from the JuSpace toolbox covering serotonergic receptors (5-HT1A, 5-HT1B, 5-HT2A, 5-HT4, 5-HT6), dopaminergic receptors (D1, D2), histamine H3 receptor, dopamine transporter (DAT), serotonin transporter (SERT), norepinephrine transporter (NET), vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT), cholinergic receptors (M1, α4β2), glutamate receptors (mGluR5, NMDA), cannabinoid CB1, opioid μ, and GABAA receptor. Three functional measures were analyzed: fALFF (fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations, 0.008-0.09 Hz), LCOR (local correlation), and GCOR (global correlation). The analysis was repeated after controlling for atrophy, with most findings remaining significant except for LCOR-5-HT1B and LCOR-VAChT associations in PD. Total intracranial volume (TIV) was recorded for the healthy cohort (mean 1.548 ± 0.152 L; females: 1.467 ± 0.116 L; males: 1.643 ± 0.133 L).
